questions.question: What is the central correctness invariant of a synchronous distributed training step?
options: Every rank contributes according to the intended batch and synchronization contract before one coherent update is published
Every GPU reports the same utilization percentage
Each rank can apply a partial optimizer update independently
Checkpoint storage is faster than GPU memory
questions.explanation: Distributed execution may partition work, but the logical optimizer step must still represent the intended data and synchronized state. A failed partial step must not be published.

questions.question: Using the lesson's 16-bytes-per-parameter mixed-precision Adam proxy, how much persistent model state does a replicated 70B model require on each DDP rank before activations?
options: 35 GB
70 GB
questions.explanation: One billion parameters times one byte is one decimal GB. Therefore 70 x 16 = 1,120 GB per fully replicated rank before activations and temporary buffers.

questions.question: Which persistent states are partitioned by ZeRO Stage 3 or full-shard FSDP in the lesson's capacity model?
options: Only the input dataset
Only optimizer moments
Optimizer state and gradients, but never parameters
Parameters, gradients, and optimizer state
questions.explanation: Full sharding partitions parameters, gradients, and optimizer state. Parameters are gathered temporarily when a module needs them, so peak memory still needs measurement.

questions.question: A job has micro-batch 2, gradient accumulation 8, data-parallel degree 16, tensor-parallel degree 4, and pipeline-parallel degree 2. What is its global batch?
questions.explanation: Global batch is 2 x 8 x 16 = 256. Tensor- and pipeline-parallel ranks collaborate on the same examples, so those degrees do not multiply the batch.

questions.question: Why can one missing or reordered NCCL collective call stall the other ranks?
options: Collectives require all participating ranks to enter compatible operations in the same order
NCCL writes every checkpoint to one GPU
All-reduce operates without process groups
Pipeline stages never communicate
questions.explanation: A collective is a group operation. Peers wait for the expected participants and operation ordering, so divergent control flow can produce an indefinite wait.

questions.question: What is the safest response when a rank fails before the current collective and optimizer step complete?
options: Apply the surviving ranks' partial gradients
Start from random weights on the replacement rank
Discard the partial step, rebuild a valid group, and restore the last committed complete checkpoint
Mark the newest incomplete checkpoint as valid
questions.explanation: The failed collective did not produce a coherent global update. Recovery should reconstruct the group and all required training state from a committed checkpoint.

questions.question: Why must a resumable training checkpoint include more than model weights?
options: Optimizer, scheduler, scaler, progress, sampler, RNG, and layout state may all change the next update
Model weights cannot be serialized
Only dashboard colors are stored outside model weights
The data position never affects training
questions.explanation: Weights alone describe parameters, not the complete continuation. Missing optimizer or progress state can change the trajectory or silently repeat and skip data.
